title: Anthropic Finalizing $15 Billion Pre-IPO Credit Facility
summary: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize expanding its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, clearing a hurdle before the artificial intelligence firm’s public filing for its highly anticipated IPO.

title: Toyota's Sato: AI Can Advance Autonomous Driving
summary: Toyota's Koji Sato says AI in mobility must be judged on two fronts: accelerating autonomous driving and boosting manufacturing productivity. He speaks exclusively with Bloomberg TV. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nomura's Goto Sees Further BOJ Rate Hikes as 'Possible'
summary: Nomura’s Yujiro Goto sees a 25-basis-point BOJ hike in September as reasonable, potentially followed by additional tightening. He adds that external pressure from the US could further influence decision makers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australian Property Developer Bathla Survives, For Now
summary: Australia's Bathla Group remains in discussions over a short-term funding deal that would avert the collapse of one of Sydney’s largest residential property developers. Bloomberg's Paul Allen reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Dollar Slumps to Start September as Yen Surges on Rate Bets
summary: The dollar slumped to start September as traders cut bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike this month and a surging yen rippled across global currency markets.

title: Gold to End Volatile Week Higher as Fedspeak Trims Rate-Hike Bet
summary: Gold steadied — after rising more than 2% on Thursday — after a Federal Reserve official’s comments on inflation helped to lower the odds of an interest-rate hike.

title: Jokowi’s Legacy of Debt May Curb Danantara’s Investment Ambition
summary: The financial strain facing some of Indonesia’s biggest state-owned construction firms, rooted in former President Joko Widodo’s infrastructure drive, risks forcing current leader Prabowo Subianto’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara to spend more to overhaul them, potentially limiting its ability to pursue new investments.

title: Malaysian Palm Oil Exports Fell in August on Weak Indian Demand
summary: Malaysian palm oil exports likely fell last month on weaker-than-usual festival demand in major buyer India.

title: Yen’s $103 Billion Short Risks Unwind Below 155, JPMorgan Says
summary: A further unwind of sizable short positions could accelerate the yen’s gains if it strengthens past 155 per dollar, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co. strategists.

title: Pacific Leaders Criticize China’s Recent Ballistic Missile Test
summary: The leaders of Pacific island nations criticized China’s recent missile test in their region, an unexpected move after earlier failed attempts to agree on a response.

title: Hong Kong’s Picky IPO Issuers Rewrite Playbook for Allocations
summary: Hong Kong’s boom in initial public offerings has turned getting shares in the hottest deals into something of an invitation-only affair.

title: SEC Moves to Nix Rule on Adviser Political Donations
summary: Investment advisers would no longer be prohibited from offering services to public pension funds if they made recent political donations to state and local elected officials, the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a proposed rule change Thursday.

title: Stocks Climb as Fed-Hike Wagers Ease on Waller: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks rose the most in a month as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be willing to support holding rates steady if price pressures continue to show signs of easing.

title: Lululemon Needs a Full Product Overhaul, Widlitz Says
summary: SW Retail Advisors President and founder Stacey Widlitz discusses Lululemon Athletica lowering its full-year outlook for a second straight quarter on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Rises as Intervention Risks, BOJ Hike Bets Jolt Traders
summary: The yen strengthened nearly 2% Thursday, reversing a month of gradual decline, as traders lifted bets on Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes and remained vigilant to the risk of official action to further boost the currency.

title: Wine Distributor Stephen Burton Gets Prison Term in Rare Vintage Scam
summary: The founder of a London wine-distribution business was sentenced in the US to six years in prison for orchestrating a scam that cost investors almost $100 million and was based on bottles of rare vintages that didn’t exist.
